# Artifact Keeper 1.11.1

A security and correctness patch release on the 1.11 line: 24 changelog entries from 11 pull requests since 1.11.0. The headline is **a client IP taken from `X-Forwarded-For` is no longer treated as authorization-grade** (#4681, GHSA-59x8-r6jj-x95h), which changes how IP-conditioned permission rules and audit attribution behave behind a reverse proxy; read the first section before upgrading. Around it are eleven more Security entries, most of them from a red-team pass over 1.11.0 (token scoping, CI OIDC, upstream credentials, log redaction, VSIX ingest and four RustSec dependency bumps), and eleven fixes, most of them in scanning and on the generic download route. **No schema migrations.** One new setting, `XFF_TRUSTED_FOR_AUTHZ`, and one new tunable, `HTTP_HEADER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECS`.

## Read this first: `allowed_cidrs` conditions and audit IPs behind a proxy

**IP-conditioned permission rules and audit-row client IPs no longer trust an X-Forwarded-For address the backend cannot verify** (#4681, GHSA-59x8-r6jj-x95h). For a request whose TCP peer is inside `RATE_LIMIT_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`, the client IP resolved from `X-Forwarded-For` was used for `allowed_cidrs` permission conditions and for the client IP recorded in audit rows. That address is only reliable when every trusted proxy appends the peer it received the request from, which the backend cannot check, so a caller who could reach the backend through a trusted proxy that passes the header through could claim any source address.

The new `XFF_TRUSTED_FOR_AUTHZ` setting (default `false`) decides whether the forwarded address may be used for these two purposes. With it unset:

- A request through a trusted proxy has an **unknown client IP for authorization and audit**. Grants with an `allowed_cidrs` condition do not match it and are denied; unconditioned grants are unaffected.
- Audit rows for such requests record no client IP.
- A request whose TCP peer is not a trusted proxy still uses that peer, as before.
- Rate limiting, the upload guard and download telemetry keep resolving the client from `X-Forwarded-For`; nothing changes there.
- Startup logs a warning when `RATE_LIMIT_TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS` is set and `XFF_TRUSTED_FOR_AUTHZ` is not.

**If you run behind a reverse proxy and use `allowed_cidrs` conditions, or you rely on the client IP in audit rows, set `XFF_TRUSTED_FOR_AUTHZ=true`**, but only after confirming that every proxy in the trusted ranges appends or overwrites `X-Forwarded-For` with its own peer address, all the way to the edge. Behind SNAT or a load balancer that hides the client address before the first proxy, no setting recovers the client IP, and a condition covering the proxy, node or pod ranges matches every proxied request. Helm chart 1.9.28 and earlier defaulted the trusted ranges to every RFC 1918 block, which trusts every pod in the cluster; the current chart defaults to none and exposes both settings as `backend.clientIp.trustedProxyCidrs` and `backend.clientIp.xffTrustedForAuthz`. `.env.example` has the full discussion.

## Read this second: requests that are now refused

- **A public Remote with upstream credentials is refused: `400 PUBLIC_REMOTE_UPSTREAM_CREDENTIALS`** (#4662). A Remote could be made public while carrying an upstream bearer token, basic credentials, AWS upstream auth or userinfo in `upstream_url`, and every anonymous request through it then spent those credentials upstream. Creating such a repository, updating one into that state, or `PUT .../upstream-auth` on a public Remote is now refused. An administrator who means it sends `allow_public_with_upstream_credentials: true`; the acceptance is stored, logged at `WARN` and audited, and repository responses report `public_with_upstream_credentials`. A repository already in that state before the upgrade keeps working and is not refused on unrelated updates, so a Terraform apply that re-sends `is_public: true` still succeeds; review repositories that now report `public_with_upstream_credentials: true`.
- **A CI OIDC provider cannot be given a Kubernetes API server's audience: `400`** (#4133). `https://kubernetes.default.svc` and `https://kubernetes.default.svc.cluster.local` accept every pod's default ServiceAccount token, and a token presented to Artifact Keeper would also be valid against the API server. Providers that already carry such an audience keep working and are named in a `security` warning at each startup; change them.
- **Repository-scoped admin tokens get `403` on `/api/v1/admin/downloads*` and `/api/v1/admin/stats`** (#4550), as `/api/v1/admin/holds/*` already did. Token scope binds ahead of admin. Unrestricted admin tokens are unaffected.
- **An expired CI OIDC assertion no longer buys a session: `401`** (#4663). The exchange accepted an assertion up to 60 s past its `exp` and minted a token with `expires_in: 0` that session validation then accepted for its own leeway. It now refuses when less than one second of validity remains. Tokens this server signs (sessions, refresh tokens, TOTP tickets) are validated without leeway and expire exactly at their `exp`. A pipeline that exchanged its token at the last moment and relied on the overlap will see a `401`; exchange earlier.
- **A `.vsix` with traversal or absolute entry names is refused at publish: `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`** (#4673). The server never extracts a VSIX, but it stored and served such an archive verbatim to clients that might.
- **Slow or silent connections are cut off after `HTTP_HEADER_READ_TIMEOUT_SECS` (default 10)** (#4665). The API and metrics listeners applied no header-read timeout, so a slow-loris client held a socket indefinitely. Each timeout increments `ak_http_header_read_timeouts_total`. **The same timer closes an idle HTTP/1 keep-alive connection after the interval**, so a reverse proxy that pools upstream connections to the backend should use an upstream idle timeout below this value, or raise it. `0` disables it. HTTP/2 and gRPC are unchanged.
- **Smaller refusals.** Starting an OCI blob upload with an over-limit `Content-Length` is `413` before any body byte is read, instead of a stream reset or a `408` from the stall watchdog (#4672). `POST /api/v1/security/findings/external` refuses a NUL byte with `400` and writes the scan row and its findings in one transaction, so a failed import no longer leaves a clean-looking `completed` scan with no findings (#4667). `POST /api/v1/sbom/environment` caps its response at 64 MiB and answers `422` past it, naming the lockfile's graphs; the new `platform` and `environment` query parameters render one graph at a time (#4670). `POST /api/v1/plugins/install/local` answers `501 NOT_IMPLEMENTED` instead of `500` (#4671).

## Read this third: behaviour that changes without an error

- **The generic download route challenges anonymous callers with `401` and accepts an API token as the Basic password** (#4654, #4593). `GET /api/v1/repositories/{key}/download/{path}` answered an uncredentialed request on a private repository with the existence-hiding `404` and no `WWW-Authenticate`, so wget, curl without pre-auth, Maven and most CI fetch helpers never sent the token they had, and `username:<api_token>` was refused on this route even when sent. It now takes the format routes' contract: `401` with Basic and Bearer challenges when there is no credential (byte-identical for a private and a nonexistent repository, so not an existence oracle), and a token presented as the Basic password resolves to its owner with scopes and repository ceiling intact. An entitled-but-wrong credential still gets `404`, `?ticket=` still works, and a browser navigation still gets only the Bearer challenge. Every other `/api/v1/*` route still refuses the token-as-Basic-password. Monitoring that keyed on this route's `404` for anonymous requests will see `401` instead.
- **The dependency scanner now asks OSV about the scanned package itself, so leaf packages can gain findings** (#4669). A package with no dependencies, such as `lodash@4.17.20`, put nothing in the advisory batch and graded `complete` with 0 findings without a single OSV request. Its own coordinates now join the batch. **Gates that passed such packages because nothing was examined can start blocking them at their next scan.** Stored results are not rewritten.
- **A repository-restricted token keeps its restriction when refreshed** (#4261). Refresh tokens now carry the repository allow-list; a restricted session no longer comes back unrestricted after one rotation. Refresh tokens issued before this release still carry no allow-list and refresh as before until they expire.
- **Download tickets and other URL-carried credentials are redacted from request-span URIs** (#4675). `ticket`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `id_token`, `client_secret`, the OIDC `code`, and presigned-URL signature parameters (`X-Amz-*`, `X-Goog-*`, `Signature`, `sig`) now log as `[REDACTED]`, matched case-insensitively after percent-decoding. Log pipelines that parsed a ticket out of the URI will no longer find one.
- **PyPI attestations published before about May 2026 verify again** (#4082). Rekor records a DSSE entry's `envelopeHash` over the envelope as submitted, and PyPI's tooling submitted spaced JSON for the first ~18 months of PEP 740, so every such attestation failed its transparency-log check and was reported as a signature or certificate-chain error. Both serializations are now accepted; a genuine mismatch is reported as `transparency log entry mismatch`. Conda CEP-27 attestations share the verification core and benefit too.
- **`storage-scrub` stops flagging every OCI manifest as corrupt** (#4666); it checks a manifest against its recorded body length instead of the image size. Real corruption is reported as before.
- **Concurrent scans of one artifact get separate workspaces** (#4668), so a re-scan during a scan or a repository rescan no longer deletes the other scan's tree. **A login refused with `429` reports the login limiter's `X-RateLimit-*` headers** rather than the API bucket's (#4664).

## Dependency updates

Four bumps for RustSec advisories that had turned Security Audit red on `main` (#4679, #4705), and one rebuild of the scanner adapter's bundled trivy for a Trivy gate finding (#4713). The first three are lockfile-only:

- `rustls` 0.23.46 (RUSTSEC-2026-0346 to -0349), the TLS stack under every outbound connection: secret leakage through `Debug`, data sent to the outer server after an ECH rejection, a 1 GiB Brotli certificate allocation before peer authentication, and a key-exchange downgrade.
- `wasmtime` 36.0.18 (RUSTSEC-2026-0352, -0363), the WASM plugin runtime: a filesystem sandbox escape via a trailing-slash symlink rename and uncapped component-model handle tables. No configuration change.
- `quinn-proto` 0.11.19 (RUSTSEC-2026-0338 to -0342), under `reqwest`'s HTTP/3 support, which the registry does not negotiate; no behaviour change.
- `zip` 9.0.4 (RUSTSEC-2026-0367 to -0369), together with `rattler_package_streaming` 0.27.15 and `rattler_conda_types` 0.57.1, because the newer streaming crate is the one built on zip 9 (#4705). The advisories cover `ZipArchive::extract()`, which the backend never calls, so no behaviour changes. One zip 2.4.2 remains in the lockfile as a build-time dependency of utoipa-swagger-ui that unpacks the vendored swagger-ui bundle during the build and is not linked into the binary; it is recorded in `.cargo/audit.toml` until utoipa-swagger-ui builds with zip 9.
- scanner-adapter 1.4.2: the bundled trivy is rebuilt as 0.74.0-r5 with containerd 2.3.4 for CVE-2026-95837 (HIGH, containerd's CRI checkpoint restore bypassing the destination security context), which had failed the image publish gate on every build since 2026-10-17 without a change in this repository (#4713). Trivy runs no CRI plugin, so scan results do not change. Upstream trivy fixes it with containerd 2.4.1 in 0.75.0 and 0.76.0; the adapter cannot take that alone because it requires the trivy server sidecar to report the same version as the bundled client, so the coordinated move of both to 0.76.0 is #4712.

The full entries are in the `## [1.11.1]` section of [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.11.1/CHANGELOG.md).
